prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
Short answer: There isn’t a single objectively “best” lawyer for every truck crash — the right attorney depends on the details of your case (injuries, at-fault parties, insurance limits, timeline) and how well the lawyer’s experience matches those needs. I can help you find a top match. Below I’ll tell you exactly how to identify the best personal injury/truck-accident lawyer in Dallas and what to ask at a free consult.

What to look for in a truck-accident lawyer
- Truck-specific experience: handled many commercial truck cases (18-wheeler, tractor-trailer, delivery trucks). Truck crashes involve federal rules (FMCSA), ELDs/black boxes, carrier safety records, and complex liability — you want an attorney who knows those issues.
- Trial experience and verdicts: many cases settle, but you want someone who will and can take the case to trial if necessary.
- Resources and staff: ability to hire accident reconstructionists, electronic-data experts, medical experts, and to cover litigation expenses until resolution.
- Board certification / peer recognition: Texas Board Certification in Personal Injury Trial Law is a strong plus; also look for Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, AV Preeminent (Martindale-Hubbell).
- Track record with similar injuries and damages: past results in catastrophic injury or wrongful death claims (if applicable).
- Communication and availability: responsive, explains strategy, assigns a clear point of contact.
- Fee structure: contingency fee percentage, who pays expenses, and when fees are deducted.
- Local knowledge: experience with Dallas courts, judges, and local defense firms can help.

Where to search and verify credentials
- Texas State Bar “Find a Lawyer” and Dallas Bar Association referral service
- Directories and ratings: Super Lawyers, Best Lawyers, Martindale-Hubbell, Avvo
- Google and Yelp reviews (read specifics, not just star ratings)
- Look up board certification on the Texas Board of Legal Specialization site
- Check disciplinary record on the Texas State Bar website

Questions to ask during the free consultation
1. How many truck-accident cases have you handled? How many in Dallas County?
2. How many of those went to trial? What were the results/settlements (examples)?
3. Do you handle these cases on contingency? What is your fee percentage and who pays costs?
4. Who will handle my case day-to-day (partner, associate, paralegal)?
5. What resources (reconstructionist, ELD analyst, medical experts) will you use?
6. What issues do you anticipate in my case (liability, comparative negligence, damages cap)?
7. How long do you expect resolution to take?
8. How often and by what method will you update me?
9. Can you provide client references or testimonials for similar cases?
10. Do you have experience dealing with the truck carrier/insurer involved in my crash?

What to bring to the consult
- Police crash report, photos, dashcam or phone videos
- Medical records and bills, ER records, prescriptions
- Insurance information (your policy and any other parties)
- Names and contact info of witnesses
- Any correspondence from insurers or businesses
- Pay stubs and proof of lost wages (if applicable)

Red flags to avoid
- Guarantees of a specific settlement amount
- Pushy pressure to sign immediately or accept a quick low offer
- Lack of trial experience or unwillingness to go to trial if needed
- Poor communication or refusal to put fee agreement in writing

Next steps I can do for you
- If you want, give me your Dallas ZIP or neighborhood and I’ll suggest 4–6 reputable firms to contact (I can’t browse now but I can guide you how to shortlist).
- I can draft a short phone script or email template to request a free consult.
- I can review names/biographies you’ve found and help pick the strongest options.

If you’d like a tailored shortlist, tell me: your ZIP code, date of crash, severity of injuries, whether the truck was commercial, and any other key facts.
